nodes.title: fix: `prefer-arrow-callback` false positive in conditional test

data.title: Bug: [prefer-arrow-callback] autofix produces a syntax error when the function is the test of a conditional
data.titleHTML: Bug: [prefer-arrow-callback] autofix produces a syntax error when the function is the test of a conditional
data.body:
### Environment

Node version: v24.16.0
npm version: v11.13.0
Local ESLint version: v10.11.0 (also reproduced on main at efc4d6bd and in the playground, v10.11.0)
Global ESLint version: Not found
Operating System: darwin 24.6.0

### What parser are you using?

Default (Espree)

### What did you do?

<details>
<summary>Configuration</summary>

```js
export default [
    {
        rules: {
            "prefer-arrow-callback": "error",
        },
    },
];
```

</details>

```js
foo(function() {} ? a : b);
```

Command:

```
printf '%s' 'foo(function() {} ? a : b);' | npx eslint --no-config-lookup --rule 'prefer-arrow-callback: error' --stdin --fix-dry-run --format json
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The fix should keep the code valid by wrapping the arrow function in parentheses:

```js
foo((() => {}) ? a : b);
```

The rule already does this when the function is an operand of a logical expression. `foo(nativeCb || function() {})` becomes `foo(nativeCb || (() => {}))`.

### What actually happened?

The fixed code does not parse. Output of the command above, trimmed to `output` and `messages`:

```json
{"output": "foo(() => {} ? a : b);", "messages": [{"ruleId": null, "fatal": true, "message": "Parsing error: Unexpected token ?", "line": 1, "column": 14}]}
```

The same happens with these inputs (same command, same trimming):

```json
{"output": "foo(() => { this; } ? a : b);", "messages": [{"ruleId": null, "fatal": true, "message": "Parsing error: Unexpected token ?", "line": 1, "column": 21}]}
{"output": "foo(bar ? () => {} ? a : b : c);", "messages": [{"ruleId": null, "fatal": true, "message": "Parsing error: Unexpected token ?", "line": 1, "column": 20}]}
{"output": "new Foo(() => {} ? a : b);", "messages": [{"ruleId": null, "fatal": true, "message": "Parsing error: Unexpected token ?", "line": 1, "column": 18}]}
{"output": "foo(async () => {} ? a : b);", "messages": [{"ruleId": null, "fatal": true, "message": "Parsing error: Unexpected token ?", "line": 1, "column": 20}]}
```

Inputs, in the same order:

- `foo(function() { this; }.bind(this) ? a : b);`
- `foo(bar ? function() {} ? a : b : c);`
- `new Foo(function() {} ? a : b);`
- `foo(async function() {} ? a : b);`

When the function is the consequent or the alternate, the output is valid: `foo(bar ? function() {} : function() {})` becomes `foo(bar ? () => {} : () => {})`.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://eslint.org/play/#

Click Fix on the `prefer-arrow-callback` message: the result is `foo(() => {} ? a : b);` with `Parsing error: Unexpected token ?` at 2:14.

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

### AI acknowledgment

- [ ] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [x] (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

### Additional comments

The fixer in `lib/rules/prefer-arrow-callback.js` skips the parentheses whenever the parent is a `ConditionalExpression`. That is right for the consequent and the alternate, but not for the test. An arrow function cannot be the test of `?:` without parentheses. I have a fix with tests ready: add the parentheses only when the replaced node is the `test` of the conditional.

node.body:
Thank for the report, I can reproduce this.

This is definitely a bug in this rule, but not because of the invalid autofix. The rule should actually not report `function() {}` in `foo(function() {} ? a : b);` because the `function() {} ? a : b` expression cannot evaluate to `function() {}`, so it shouldn't be considered as an argument/callback. PR to fix this is welcome.

commit.message:
fix(linter/eslint/prefer-arrow-callback): ignore functions used as conditional tests (#27533)

## Why

`oxlint --fix` currently turns valid code into a syntax error here
(oxlint 1.87.0, checked with `node --check`):

```js
foo(function() {} ? a : b);        // -> foo(() => {} ? a : b);        SyntaxError
new Foo(function() {} ? a : b);    // -> new Foo(() => {} ? a : b);    SyntaxError
foo(async function() {} ? a : b);  // -> foo(async () => {} ? a : b);  SyntaxError
```

ESLint had the same bug (eslint/eslint#21368) and fixed it in
eslint/eslint#21373 by not treating a function in the test of a
conditional as a callback. This ports that fix.

Found while running ESLint's upstream test file for this rule through
oxlint.

## Problem

`get_callback_info` kept walking up through a `ConditionalExpression`
even when the function was the conditional's `test`. A function used as
a test is not the callback, the conditional's result is. ESLint treats
these as valid (tests/lib/rules/prefer-arrow-callback.js L52-L59).

Before, oxlint reported `Unexpected function expression` for each of
these:

```js
foo(function() {} ? a : b);
foo(function() { this; }.bind(this) ? a : b);
foo(bar ? function() {} ? a : b : c);
new Foo(function() {} ? a : b);
```

After, none are reported. Functions in the consequent or alternate are
still callbacks, for example `foo(bar ? function() {} : function() {})`
is still reported and fixed.

## Changes

- In the `ConditionalExpression` arm, stop when the node is the `test`.
Only continue for the consequent and alternate.
- Add the eight upstream valid cases (L52-L59) to the pass vector. No
snapshot change, since only pass cases were added.

## Testing

`cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib prefer_arrow_callback`, `cargo fmt`,
`cargo clippy -p oxc_linter --all-targets -- -D warnings` all pass.

---
Written with the help of an agent (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5
orchestrating claude-sonnet-5-5).

---------
